<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The script `beammp.sh` is a launcher script that sets up a user-specific copy of the BeamMP-Launcher binary from a system-wide location (`/usr/lib/beammp/`) into a user data directory under `$XDG_DATA_HOME` or `~/.local/share`. It ensures the user copy is executable and up-to-date by comparing it with the system version using `cmp -s`, then copying if necessary with `install -m755`. This is a common pattern to allow user-specific execution without requiring elevated privileges for every run.

The script uses standard, safe practices: it creates a directory if needed, compares files byte-for-byte, and installs with predictable permissions. It then changes into the data directory and execs the launcher with all original arguments. There are no network operations, no use of dangerous functions like `eval`, no obfuscation, and no attempts to exfiltrate data or modify system files outside the user's home directory. All paths are constructed from standard environment variables with safe fallbacks.

The operations are confined to user-writable locations and the system-wide read-only installation directory. The behavior aligns with normal packaging and runtime practices for desktop applications on Linux, particularly those distributed via AUR. No malicious or suspicious behavior is present.
</details>
<evidence>
